Items.Authors: David Polishook, Eran Ofek, Sagi Ben-Ami, Ofer Yaron, Ruslan Konno, Simone Garrappa, Oren Ironi, Yahel Sofer-Rimlat, Alex Bichkovsky, Alexander Krassikchtchikova, Arie Blumenzweig, Enrico Segre, Michael Engel, Ofir Hershko, Omer Oreg
Items.Title: The new Weizmann Astrophysical Observatory (WAO)
Items.Abstract: The Weizmann Astrophysical Observatory is a new facility constructed and operated by the Weizmann Institute of Science (code M01; 35.041°E, 30.053°N; 400 m). The observatory focuses on arrays of small telescopes to demonstrate that such arrays can outperform a single seeing-limited large telescope of equal collecting area. The site will ultimately host 100 telescopes across two major arrays, the Large Array Survey Telescopes (LAST) and the Multi-Aperture Spectroscopic Telescope (MAST).

Items.Authors: Kristin K. Madsen, Andrew Ptak, Kimberly Banks, Simon Bandler, Barbara Grofic, Abe Falcone, Sven Herrmann, Steven Allen
Items.Title: The status of US NASA contributions to NewAthena
Items.Abstract: The ESA L-class mission, the Advanced Telescope for High Energy Astrophysics (Athena), was chosen for the Cosmic Vision program in 2014 to study the Hot and Energetic X-ray Universe. It was recently reformulated into NewAthena, a modified version of the original Athena. NASA has contributed to the technology and science since the early selection, and most recently, due to the redefinition, increased the scope of the contribution. The major hardware contribution is the kilo-pixel sensor for the X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) and the readout circuits for it based on time-division multiplexing (TDM) with superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs). NASA will also contribute the 4K cryocooler for the X-IFU and a vibration isolation system. AAdditional contributions include *support for* the Science Ground Segment *, design consultation* for the Wide Field Imager (WFI) *readout* ASIC and background analysis modeling for the WFI.

Items.Authors: Richard D. Stelter, Andrew Skemer, Steph Sallum, Nicholas K. Mac Donald, Renate Kupke, Christopher Ratliff, Ravinder Banyal, Thirupati Sivarani, Michael P. Fitzgerald, Emily Plume, Marc Kassis, Olivier Abseil, Natasha Batalha, Marc-Andre Boucher, Cyril Bourgenot, Will Deich, Devika Divakar, Michael Gonzales, Thomas Greene, Amirul Hasan, Phil Hinz, Becky Jensen-Clem, Chris Johnson, Govinda K. V., Isabel J. Kain, Mackenzie Lach, Jean-Thomas Landry, Jim Lyke, Ken Magone, Eduardo Marin, Rosalie McGurk, Raquel M. Martinez, Dimitri Mawet, Dale Sandford, Ramya Sethuam, Arun Surya, Eric Wang, Peyton Benac
Items.Title: Update on SCALES: the slicer combined with array of lenslets for exoplanet spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: We give an update on the status of the thermal infrared (2-5 micron) low- to mid-spectral resolution (R=lambda/delta_lambda~20-5,000), lenslet-based, integral-field spectrograph and 1-5 micron imager, the Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Science (SCALES). SCALES is deployed at the W. M. Keck Observatory behind the Keck II telescope’s Adaptive Optics (AO) system, and delivers diffraction-limited performance across its bandpass. The instrument has several key design features, including a selectable-wavelength monochromator for wavelength calibration; homologous construction of its bench, mechanisms, mounts, and optics; a slicer reimager to provide a discontinuous pseudoslit for mid-resolution spectroscopy; and a large, static lenslet array with two sub-arrays of lenslets used to feed a common spectrograph for both low- and mid-resolution modes. Since the 2024 SPIE meeting, SCALES has been fully integrated at UCSC and is expected to achieve first light in Spring 2026.

Items.Authors: Andreea Petric, Sarah Kendrew, Alberto Noriega-Crespo, Bryan Holler, Jane Morrison, Jonathan Aguillar, Stacey Alberts, Dean Hines, Greg Sloan
Items.Title: Wide field slitless spectroscopy with JWST's MIRI
Items.Abstract: Massively multiplexed spectroscopy enables efficient, statistically robust surveys of large cosmic volumes. Space-based wide-field slitless spectroscopy reduces cosmic variance by covering extensive sky areas with consistent sensitivity and calibration. In Cycle 5, JWST introduced a new MIRI prime observing mode—Wide Field Slitless Spectroscopy (WFSS)—which utilizes the P750L double prism to deliver low-resolution (R ~ 100) spectroscopy from 5 to 14 μm across an unobstructed 74″ × 113″ field of view. We present the MIRI WFSS calibration plans and their expected accuracy. We utilized established slitless-spectroscopy techniques from HST and JWST, archival P750L and MIRI imaging data, and dedicated calibration observations for flux/trace and wavelength calibration, including adjustments for positional dependencies. We present the most recent calibration reference files used for flat-fielding, background subtraction, and flux and wavelength calibration, and outline improvement plans.

Items.Authors: Aafaque R. Khan, William Verts, Harrison Bradley, Nazende Kerkeser, Daniel Turong, Elijah Garcia, Heejoo Choi, Haeun Chung, Daewook Kim, Carlos Vargas, Erika Hamden, Dave Hamara, Hannah Tanquary, Tom McMahon
Items.Title: Precision optical alignment of the Aspera far-ultraviolet (FUV) spectrographs using computer-generated hologram (CGH) interferometry and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) techniques
Items.Abstract: Aspera is a NASA SmallSat carrying two far-ultraviolet (FUV) spectrographs to detect O VI emission near 1032 Å from the circumgalactic medium. The payload has a compact opto-mechanical layout and requires tight alignment tolerances and stringent contamination-control procedures. We report a multiphase optical alignment approach using computer-generated hologram (CGH) interferometry and FUV vacuum alignment. Reflective optics and gratings were aligned with a Zygo Fizeau interferometer and custom CGH in a class-1000 cleanroom under nitrogen purge. The two slits were aligned confocal with the off-axis parabola focus using a microscope system referenced to the Zygo laser spot, and the spacecraft star tracker was aligned to the instrument boresight with a 3D scanner. Final detector alignment and focus were performed in a vacuum VUV facility using a collimator, monochromator, and hollow-cathode flow lamp. The alignment is complete, and the instrument in preparation for launch in 2026.

Items.Authors: Florentin Millour, Bruno Lopez, Romain Petrov, Anthony Soulain, Philippe Bério, Alexis Matter, James Leftley, Julien Woillez, Jens Kammerer, Sylvestre Lacour, Jean-Baptiste Lebouquin, Walter Jaffe, Stéphane Lagarde, The MATISSE Team
Items.Title: MATISSE in the Laser Guide Stars Era: updated performance with the new GPAO adaptive optics, its LGS, and a new version of its DRS
Items.Abstract: We provide an overview of MATISSE at the VLTI in the context of GRAVITY+, following its performance update following the installation of GPAO in 2024 and LGS in 2025. We summarize the key instrumental features and observing modes, global data-reduction options, the new ergonomics of the user-friendly DRS, measurable quantities, and performance. MATISSE can be operated alone or with the GRAVITY fringe tracker in the so-called GRA4MAT mode. We present the updated MATISSE performance with GRA4MAT. When using the UTs, the added capabilities of GPAO and LGS are boosting the performance.

Items.Authors: Philippe Peille, Christophe Daniel, Vincent Albouys, Didier Barret, Aurora Simionescu, Luigi Piro, Massimo Cappi
Items.Title: Technical status of the X-ray Integral Field Unit before mission adoption
Items.Abstract: The X-ray Integral field Unit is an X-ray microcalorimeter, planned to be launched on the newAthena mission. With a cryostat passively cooled to 50 K, the heart of the instrument is organized within a 4K Core. This ensemble, cooled by a remote cryocooler, contains the Focal Plane Assembly (FPA) and the Multi-stage ADR (MAX), which provides the 50 mK cooling required by the detectors.   Approaching mission adoption, the architecture is being consolidated. In this contribution, we give an overview of the instrument technical status, emphasizing the main trade-offs that were conducted. This is followed by a summary of the demonstration activities performed at system level, focusing on the role of the 4K Core DM. This model will integrate demonstration versions of the FPA, MAX, but also of the cold harness. The cold detection chain, populated at the level of 1/4th of the flight model, will be read out by a set of demonstration models of the Warm Front-End and Digital Readout Electronics.

Items.Authors: Andrea Scaudo, Matteo Genoni, Marco Landoni
Items.Title: A3I: an AI-assisted optical alignment framework for spectrographs
Items.Abstract: We present A3I (Artificial Intelligence Assisted Alignment and Integration), a deep-learning framework that analyzes detector images to detect misalignments in key optical elements and suggest corrective actions. Designed to support instrument teams during Assembly, Integration and Testing, A3I provides rapid, data-driven feedback. In its first application to the NIR arm of SOXS, A3I is trained on simulated calibration frames from an End-to-End spectrograph simulator, perturbing three main components across 15 alignment-related degrees of freedom. It achieves about 79% overall accuracy and nearly 90% on the most critical degrees of freedom, highlighting its potential as a portable decision-support tool.

Items.Authors: Dongok Ryu, Youngchun Youk, Goeun Kim, Jongguk Choe, Shinwook Kim, Min Seok Kim, Jeeyeon Yoon, EungShik Lee, Haeng Pal Heo
Items.Title: Digital-twin-based end-to-end verification of space telescopes using Earth-observation camera heritage
Items.Abstract: Earth-observation cameras and space telescopes share similar front-end optics but differ in focal-plane design and observing modes. Earth-observation payloads use compact telescopes with push-broom line detectors for bright targets and long swaths, while space telescopes use area detectors, long staring observations, and shared focal planes for faint-source instruments. To extend Earth-observation test methods, we use a full-aperture collimator and knife-edge target system, originally developed for push-broom MTF measurement, to obtain pixel-level PSFs for telescope-class instruments. A non-sequential digital twin is built by modeling the target, collimator, and telescope optics and adding measured mirror surfaces, alignment data, gravity effects, CFRP thermal-vacuum behavior, and focus mechanism response. Calibrated with Earth-observation heritage data, the model predicts ground, thermal-vacuum, and on-orbit performance within a unified framework.

Items.Authors: Benjamin J.S. Pope, Louis Desdoigts, Max Charles, Peter Tuthill
Items.Title: End-to-end modelling and speckle subtraction with the JWST NIRCam coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The limiting noise floor in almost all coronagraphic observations is from uncertainty in the field of speckles around a bright star, in which optical aberrations can easily hide a faint planet. Data-driven methods for subtracting this field have been very successful, but the exquisite precision of the James Webb Space Telescope instruments implies much deeper fundamental contrast and resolution limits than are routinely being achieved. Recent advances in differentiable optics models and machine learning have made it possible to simulate and perform phase retrieval on the optical system end-to-end, trained on science data, and provide much more accurate predictive models of the speckle field in the James Webb NIRISS Interferometer. We present the early results of adapting these methods to the NIRCam coronagraph, achieving improvements in wavefront sensing and metrology and a path to deeper coronagraphy with JWST and other space telescopes.

Items.Authors: Anastasia Alexov, Eric Christensen, Bruno Quint, David Sanmartim, Alysha Shugart, Kevin Reil, Keith Bechtol, Robert Lupton, Holger Drass, Yusra AlSayyad, Gonzalo Aravena, Erik Dennihy, Lukas Eisert, Parker Fagrelius, Kevin Fanning, Guillem Megias Homar, Minhee Hyun, Bryce Kalmbach, Yijung Kang, Kshitija Kelkar, Narayan Khadka, Craig Lage, Paulo Lago, Shuang Liang, Joshua Meyers, Carlos Morales, Kristopher Mortensen, Kate Napier, HyeYun Park, Marina Pavlović, Karla Peña, Bekah Polen, Tiago Ribeiro, Jacqueline Seron, Colin Slater, Brian Stalder, Chris Suberlak, Sandrine Thomas, Elana Urbach, Paulina Venegas, Danica Žilková
Items.Title: Lessons learned from nighttime commissioning the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory: operational models, support, shifts and workflows - the good, the bad and the …
Items.Abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory completed construction and transitioned to operations on October 25, 2025. This paper summarizes key lessons from the System Integration, Test and Commissioning (SIT-Com) phase. Early project-wide staffing ramp-up proved essential for the intensive testing campaigns, including formalized shift structures and on-site roles. The Auxiliary Telescope served as a critical pathfinder, reducing risk and accelerating commissioning of the Simonyi Survey Telescope. Effective commissioning required a targeted surge of staff and careful planning of on-site presence. Tools such as Google Sheets supported workflow management, scheduling, and evolving automation. The nearly year-long sprint of commissioning highlighted challenges in staffing, fatigue, and coordination, informing Rubin’s transition from an unsustainable sprint mode to a sustainable 10-year LSST operations model.

Items.Authors: Nathan P. Lourie, Stefan Lauxtermann, Daniel P. Kelly, Jill Juneau, Edward Cheng, Gábor Furész, Jonathan Mah, Laddawan Miko, Gregory Mosby, Peter C. Nagler, Gustav Pettersson, Per-Olov Pettersson, Robert A. Simcoe
Items.Title: MOSAIC-4k6k: development of a large-format InGaAs focal plane array for infrared astronomy
Items.Abstract: Wide-field infrared time domain astronomy is limited by the high cost of large format scientific detectors. We present progress towards a new large-format, low-cost SWIR detector: the Megapixel Optical/Infrared Sensor for Astronomical Imaging & Characterization (MOSAIC) InGaAs FPA with a 4k x 6k 10 micron format, called the MOSAIC-4k6k. Using lattice matched InGaAs, we expect high quantum efficiency from 0.8 microns (0.4 microns with substrate removal) up to its 1.7 micron (room temperature) cutoff, and target a dark current of <0.1 e/pixel/s at 150 K. We present the MOSIAC-4k6k concept, a novel hybridization approach to reduce material costs, on-sky results from a pathfinder InGaAs camera, and progress towards cryogenic demonstration of the first 4k x 6k ROICs.

Items.Authors: Alexei Pevtsov, Christoph Keller, Mark Warner, Luca Bertello, Sanjay Gosain, Roth Markus, Michael Sigwarth, Thomas Berger
Items.Title: Next generation ground based solar observing network
Items.Abstract: The US National Science Foundation recently funded the design of the next generation Ground-based Solar Observing Network (ngGONG) consisting of 6 robotic stations around the globe that will provide continuous observations of the magnetic field, Doppler velocities, narrowband images, and sun-as-a-star measurements for solar synoptic research and operational space weather forecasting. To understand the solar cycle and dynamo, ngGONG will have an operational lifetime of two complete magnetic cycles (about 50 years). ngGONG will expand the boundaries in investigating subsurface flows in the solar convection zone to larger depths and higher latitudes than is currently done. It will provide full vector magnetic fields at several heights in the solar atmosphere, thus improving our understanding of the upward flow of magnetic energy and helicity. This presentation will give an overview of the conceptual design of ngGONG and the requirements for its operations.

Items.Authors: Mary Joe Medlej, Rahul Srinivasan, Simon Prunet, Aziz Ziad, Christophe Giordano
Items.Title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Short-Term Atmospheric Seeing Forecasting
Items.Abstract: Predicting atmospheric and turbulence conditions has become increasingly crucial for both the astronomical community and free-space optical communications. With the advent of the next generation of extremely large telescopes and sensitive optical links, accurate forecasts are needed to mitigate degradation caused by turbulence. To address these challenges, this work focuses on optimizing turbulence prediction across two complementary timescales: long-term ground-layer forecasts using numerical simulations constrained by in-situ drone measurements in the first 450 m, and short-term forecasts using machine learning with a focus on probabilistic models.

Items.Authors: Ruben Tandon, Lucas Marquis, Liurong Lin, Derya Öztürk Çetni, Axel Potier, Audrey Baur, Iljadin Manurung, Mathias Brändli, Martin Rieder, Daniele Piazza, Laurent Jolissaint, Jonas G. Kühn
Items.Title: The PLACID active coronagraphic imager instrument: commissioning status
Items.Abstract: The world’s first adaptive stellar coronagraph, the Programmable Liquid-crystal Active Coronagraphic Imager for the 4-m DAG telescope (PLACID) uses a spatial light modulator operating from H- to Ks-band to dynamically adjust the focal-plane phase mask entirely in software. Positioned between the TROIA XAO system and the DIRAC infrared detector, PLACID was internally aligned on the Nasmyth platform of the Turkish 4-m DAG telescope in 2026 and shall be on-sky by mid/late 2026. When ready, it will perform high-contrast imaging of exoplanets, brown dwarfs, disks, and binary systems, being able to easily deploy any desired phase pattern in the focal plane. Upcoming features include self-calibration of non-common path aberrations, coronagraphic nulling of binary-stars, and coherent differential imaging. We present the finalized GUI, discovery-space estimates, internal alignment results, observation tools and prepared data reduction software, to be ready for first science by early 2027.

Items.Authors: Baptiste Besnard, Damien Gratadour, Etienne Bonnassieux, Marwane Dalal, Javier Conejero, Raül Sirvent, Rosa Badia
Items.Title: Towards a scalable and composable end-to-end workflow for radio-interferometric imaging
Items.Abstract: Developing a fully composable and pipelined workflow became essential to handle SKA-scale data-intensive tasks. By integrating interoperable tools, orchestrated by a resource-optimization manager, the platform can efficiently leverage SKA data. Its flexible design supports the incorporation of future AI algorithms for solving inverse imaging problems or proposing alternative reconstruction methods.

Items.Authors: E. Soria, M. Núñez-Cagigal, A. Mato, L. Montoya, N. Rodríguez-Linares, N. Feijóo, M. Barreto
Items.Title: Adaptive optics for EST first light: system architecture and calibration concept
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) is a 4.2-m solar facility designed to achieve diffraction-limited performance from the visible to the near-infrared. Given the challenges of daytime atmospheric turbulence, adaptive optics plays a central role in enabling its scientific capabilities. Here we present the design of the first-light AO system, based on a single-conjugate architecture, together with its complete calibration framework, establishing the baseline system after the PDR and paving the way towards the future multi-conjugate AO implementation.

Items.Authors: Stephen J. Smith, Joseph S. Adams, Simon R. Bandler, James A. Chervenak, Felipe A. Colazo-Petit, Tannaz Farrahi, Fred M. Finkbeiner, Joshua D. Fuhrman, Samuel V. Hull, Richard L. Kelley, Caroline A. Kilbourne, Haruka Muramatsu, Frederick S. Porter, Asha Rani, Kazuhiro Sakai, Ambarish C. Venkatasubramani, Nicholas A. Wakeham, Edward J. Wassell, Michael C. Witthoeft, Sang H. Yoon
Items.Title: Development of the microcalorimeter detector for the NewAthena/X-ray integral field unit
Items.Abstract: The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) will be a microcalorimeter instrument on ESA’s NewAthena X-ray observatory, set to launch in the late 2030's. The X-IFU will consist of 1,504 transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters read out via time-division multiplexing (TDM). We report recent progress in developing these detectors, including the design, fabrication, and characterization of the first full-scale, flight-representative array produced at NASA GSFC. This array has completed initial performance testing—covering spectral resolution, uniformity, and noise behavior—and is now under evaluation in the European FPA Development Model. Additional arrays have undergone environmental qualification, including vibration and thermal-cycle testing, demonstrating mechanical robustness. We also outline ongoing improvements in design and fabrication process refinements as part of our development towards the implementation of an Engineering Model detector.

Items.Authors: Mathias Nowak, Sylvestre Lacour, Elsa Huby, Tristan Buey, Jehanne Sarrazin, Amira Bouikni, Senol Yazici
Items.Title: Upgrading PIONIER for dual-field interferometry in the J Band
Items.Abstract: We present PLANETES, an upgrade of the VLTI instrument PIONIER that brings GRAVITY-style dual-field interferometry into the J band. Building on PIONIER’s legacy in high-resolution near-infrared imaging and GRAVITY’s breakthroughs in dual-field operation, the upgraded instrument integrates dual-field injection, a new metrology system, and an integrated-optics ABCD combiner. This capability will enable high-contrast studies of giant planets near the ice line, accretion processes traced by hydrogen lines in young planets, and reflected-light detections of mature exoplanets. First laboratory tests of the metrology concept are presented, along with the long-term prospects for future short-wavelength VLTI instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Gloria Mellinand, Diane Chapuis Kerouanton, Malak Galal, Sébastien Pernecker, Rémi Giroud, Alexandre Jeanneau, Florence Laurent, Johan Richard, Chris Coote, Jon Moller, Jean-Paul Kneib, Eirini Tagkoudi
Items.Title: Motorized mount for the 3-DoF folding mirrors of the VLT’s BlueMUSE instrument
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimized, medium spectral resolution, panoramic integral field spectrograph under development for the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The project is now fully entering design phase. With an optimized transmission down to 350 nm, spectral resolution of R 3500 on average across the wavelength range, and a large FoV (1 arcmin²), BlueMUSE will open up a new range of galactic and extragalactic science cases facilitated by its specific capabilities.  To meet the stability demands required for BlueMUSE, motorized mounts for precise and repeatable positioning of key optics are developed. This paper explores candidate mechanical designs for BlueMUSE’s Folding Mirror 2 (FM2), a high-precision mirror mount with three degrees-of-freedom: tip, tilt rotations, and vertical translation. The study includes a comparative performance analysis through simulations, the overall architecture of the chosen design, and the dedicated optical setup built to characterize FM2's performance.

Items.Authors: Eric Villard, Michele Delli Veneri, Eric Emsellem, Fabrizia Guglielmetti, John Hibbard, Mark Lacy, Marcella Massardi, Brett McGuire, Emanuela Orrú, Roberto Pizzo, Felix Stoehr, Peter Teuben, Stefan Wijnholds, Martin Zwaan
Items.Title: Advanced data products for radio observatories
Items.Abstract: Advanced Data Products (ADPs) are increasingly central to enhancing the efficiency and scientific output of radio observatories. Designed to bridge the gap between raw observational data and science-ready results, ADPs reduce processing overhead, improve reproducibility, and enable a wider range of researchers to engage with complex datasets. Their benefits include accelerated research, interoperability across archives, and reduced duplication of computational effort, with direct implications for sustainability.  This presentation summarizes the outcomes of the ADP2024 workshop, which reviewed current practices at major facilities including ALMA, SKAO, LOFAR, VLA, and ESO. We highlight lessons learned from ongoing initiatives. Critical issues identified include standardization, provenance tracking, quality assurance, and long-term maintenance. We conclude that ADPs represent a key step toward sustainable, accessible, and scientifically optimized data ecosystems in radio astronomy.

Items.Authors: Weimin Sun, Jinhui Cui, Dongsheng Hu, Haojie Yang, Chuanqi Chen, Yichen Li, Tao Jiang, Shuqing Wang, Ali Luo
Items.Title: AI assisted astronomical spectral processing based on distortion correction
Items.Abstract: In fiber-fed multi-object astronomical spectroscopy, each spectrograph records two-dimensional spectral images from hundreds of fibers. We present an AI-assisted processing framework that integrates subpixel distortion correction, deep learning-based noise identification, two-dimensional fiber-spot reconstruction, and spectral de-blending. For spectral images acquired with FASOT, a maximum Keystone displacement of 24.79 pixels was corrected to subpixel accuracy, with 87.4% of residuals below 0.10 pixels. The CNN classifier achieved 99.2% accuracy, and the YOLOv8-S model reached 98.1% mAP@0.5 for pixel-level noise localization. Among 250 fibers of LAMOST, 95.6% exhibited smooth single-peaked spots, while 4.4% showed central depressions indicative of coupling defects. For overlapped spectra, the recovered spectra closely matched the reference spectra, demonstrating effective suppression of inter-fiber crosstalk. A FITS-based processing platform was developed and successfully applied.

Items.Authors: Pierre Jouve, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Carlos Correia, Andrew Rakich, Julien Charton, Jon Lawrence, Yizheng Wang, Michael Goodwin, Eduard Muslimov
Items.Title: AOB-WAN: the new adaptive optics bench at GEMINI North
Items.Abstract: AOB-WAN is an Adaptive Optics facility feeding the GIRMOS instrument on the Gemini North 8-m telescope. It operates in a single AO mode with a fixed LGS asterism, using an LTAO reconstruction with four LGS and one to three NGS. The reconstructed wavefront can be projected over various FoV sizes: high performance is achieved on a narrow field, while larger fields up to 2′ yield moderate correction. The system incorporates recent advances in multi-LGS tomography, including super-resolution techniques and on-sky calibration. For the full 2′ FoV, a second correction stage is provided by the MOAO mode within GIRMOS. The architecture is designed for high sky coverage, reaching up to 60% at the North Galactic Pole. AOB-WAN is conceived as a fast-track, cost-effective project targeting first light by 2028, combining innovative concepts with reliable, well-controlled components. This paper presents the design, performance analysis, and initial AIT results.

Items.Authors: Miguel A. Núñez Cagigal, Alvaro Perez, Jorge Quintero, Angel Mato, Juan Cozar, Hector Socas, David Barr, Josue Barrera, Mary Barreto, Marta Belio, Adrian Calzadilla, Yanira Carballo, Manuel Collados, John Connolly, Gonzalo Moran, Thomas Davies, Sofia Dimoudi, Andrew Dunn, Noelia Feijóo, Pedro García-Martín, Sergio González-Manrique, Kelemu Helawae, Angela Hernandez-Delgado, Javier León-Gil, Ana Marcos, Yolanda Martín-Hernando, Alejandra Martín-Galvez, Fernando Merlos, Luz Maria Montoya, Tim Morris, Nicolás Rodriguez-Linares, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Mahy Soler, Esther Soria, Antonio Zamora
Items.Title: European Solar Telescope Status: Progressing from Preliminary Design to Detailed Design
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) will be the largest solar telescope in Europe with a primary mirror of 4.2 m in diameter and it will be built in the Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos (ORM).     EST has successfully passed its Preliminary Design Reviews (PDRs) structured in seven reviews from October 2024 to December 2025 covering all disciplines. The review panels were composed of a total of 29 international reviewers who had not made previous contributions to EST. During 2026, EST continues implementing the corrective actions identified during the reviews to move forward to the detailed design and construction phases. This paper reports the lessons learned during the reviews, a description of the EST design and the next steps towards the EST construction.

Items.Authors: Takehiko Wada, Toshihiro Nakaoka, Toyoaki Suzuki, Youta Tanaka
Items.Title: Proof-of-concept of a monolithic mid-infrared image sensor “IR-SOIPIX” using standard CMOS process
Items.Abstract: IR-SOIPIX is a monolithic mid-infrared (MIR) image sensor developed using a standard CMOS process on a silicon-on-insulator wafer. Unlike conventional hybrid detectors that require indium bump bonding, IR-SOIPIX integrates the detector and readout circuitry in a single chip, reducing complexity and cost. Cryogenic tests (~4 K) on a single-element test device confirmed key features: dark current suppression using a blocking layer, identification of impurity-related activation energies, and photon detection up to ~30 μm. The initial prototype demonstrated a quantum efficiency of about 1%, and further optimization of impurity concentration and layer thickness is expected to improve this by up to an order of magnitude. These results establish the feasibility of scalable, low-cost MIR sensors for next-generation astronomical missions.

Items.Authors: Christophe Lovis, Nicolas Blind, Bruno Chazelas, Muskan Shinde, Maddalena Bugatti, Nathanaël Restori, Isaac Dinis, Ludovic Genolet, Ian Hughes, Michaël Sordet, Robin Schnell, Samuel Rihs, Adrien Crausaz, Léonie Hoerner, Bachar Wehbe, Mary Angelie M. Alagao, Sylvain Cetre, Romain Fetick, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Taïssir Heritier, Vincent Chambouleyron, Mathilde Houelle, Emeline Bolmont, Martin N. Turbet, Thibaud Frutig, Sandrine Guerlet, Joshua Blackman, Christoph Mordasini, Brice-Olivier Demory, David Ehrenreich
Items.Title: RISTRETTO status update and science cases for high-contrast spectroscopy at the diffraction limit of the VLT
Items.Abstract: RISTRETTO is a visible high-resolution spectrograph fed by an extreme adaptive optics (AO) system, to be  proposed as a visitor instrument on ESO VLT. The main science goal of RISTRETTO is to pioneer the detection and atmospheric characterisation of exoplanets in reflected light, in particular the temperate rocky planet  Proxima b. RISTRETTO will be able to measure albedos and detect atmospheric features in a number of exoplanets orbiting nearby stars for the first time. It will do so by combining a high-contrast AO system working  at the diﬀraction limit of the telescope to a high-resolution spectrograph, via a 7-spaxel integral-field unit (IFU)  feeding single-mode fibers. Further science cases for RISTRETTO include the study of accreting protoplanets through spectrally-resolved H-alpha emission, and protoplanetary disks kinematics via Doppler measurements. In this talk we will present laboratory and on-sky tests of the spectrograph, coronagraphic IFU, and Pyramid WFS sub-systems.

Items.Authors: Cèdre Mercier, Ugo Tricoli, Jean-François Sauvage, Cyril Petit, benoit neichel
Items.Title: Towards Stereoscopic inversion of visible light curves for non-cooperative satellite attitude retrieval
Items.Abstract: We investigate how stereoscopic unresolved photometry can improve attitude reconstruction for Resident Space Objects observed in the visible band. Using ENVISAT light curves acquired with the ONERA FEELINGS telescope, we first perform single-site inversions and highlight their intrinsic ambiguities due to viewing geometry, BRDF effects and phase angle. We then introduce a fast forward photometric model, SIRIUS, that couples high-resolution shapes, material-dependent BRDFs, full attitude dynamics and the GPU-based renderer to generate consistent multi-station light curves. Using this framework, we explore a dual-station configuration and show on complex, non-symmetric shapes that differential scattering between sites can better constrain spin period, rotation-axis orientation and initial angular state. These exploratory results underline the feasibility and added value of unresolved stereoscopic acquisitions for future SSA networks relying on optical measurements only.

Items.Authors: Sylvain Martin, Anthony Attard, Florian Bancel, Ivan Charles, Jean-Louis Durand, Adèle Léon, Christophe Martin, Adeline Robert, Elise Bellouard, Jean-Marc Duval
Items.Title: 5-stages ADR cooler for the Athena space mission: toward the demonstration model for X-IFU
Items.Abstract: The ATHENA L-class mission from the European Space Agency (ESA) aim to study the hot and energetic universe. The very highly sensitive X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) needs temperature as low as 50 mK. From a 5 K interface, CEA developed a succession of 5 ADR (Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigerator) stages that provides cooling interface at 1.8 K, 320 mK and 50 mK for the focal plane assembly. A demonstration model (DM) has been designed following integration constraint on X-IFU. Test results will be presented before final integration in the X-IFU 4K – core DM model at CNES as well as next steps towards the FM model.

Items.Authors: Alicia M. Anderson, Samantha J. Thompson, Eugene B. Seneta, Alireza Esmaeilzadeh, Clark E. Baker, John S. Young
Items.Title: Design and evaluation of a white-LED ring for uniform CCD flat-field and contamination monitoring in HARPS3
Items.Abstract: he High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher–3 (HARPS3) is being developed for the 10-year Terra Hunting Experiment. Achieving 10 cm s⁻¹ radial-velocity precision requires detailed characterisation of detector behaviour, where uniform flat-field illumination is essential for identifying pixel-to-pixel variations and surface defects that can introduce spurious spectral features. We present the HARPS3 flat-field light source: an LED ring mounted between the camera objective and the CCD, designed to uniformly illuminate the full detector, including inter-order regions. The system uses white LEDs to better represent broadband optical throughput and incorporates interchangeable diffusion elements to reduce flux and improve spatial uniformity. Laboratory measurements across multiple configurations are presented, and we identify the optimal setup for calibration products and long-term CCD health monitoring.

Items.Authors: Antoine Mérand
Items.Title: Status and future of the VLTI
Items.Abstract: As of 2026, high performance adaptive optics, laser guide stars and off-axis capabilities have been implemented under the GRAVITY+ project, opening unique scientific frontiers by offering unprecedented sensitivity and sky coverage, in both galactic and extra-galactic domains.     The coming years will see the realization of these opportunities, and the success will also be measured by bringing access to a broader community. In the short term, VLTI has still room to go beyond its current capabilities: the infrastructure still limits performances (e.g. vibration control), and new avenues are being explored with visitor instruments (shorter wavelength, nulling, alternate fringe tracking strategies, etc.). In the medium term, ESO is establishing a roadmap for the instrument developments of VLT and VLTI with the “VLT Beyond 2030” exercise: several projects have been proposed, demonstrating the community engagement, and that VLTI has still a big potential for the coming decades.

Items.Authors: Márton Koren, Sébastien Vievard, Branden Allen
Items.Title: Computational fluid dynamics–based modeling of the low wind effect and its impact on high-contrast imaging at the Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Low Wind Effect (LWE) significantly degrades high-contrast imaging at the Subaru Telescope. This work introduces a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) based simulation framework using OpenFOAM to model airflow, thermal behavior, and resulting optical distortions under various wind and telescope orientations. The setup includes a summit-scale model, a detailed telescope-and-dome model, and a vent-cover model for implicit parameterization. Optical path differences from the CFD output are propagated through an optical simulation to assess coronagraphic contrast. The study also examines mitigation concepts such as spider coatings. Results identify key conditions that trigger LWE and highlight promising mitigation approaches.

Items.Authors: Jifeng Liu, Meng Sun, Liang Ge, Yang Huang, Yi Hu, Lei Jia, Wenxiong Li, Zhengyang Li, Ning-Chen Sun, Hu Zou
Items.Title: The GOTTA Project: a Global Telescope Network for Transients
Items.Abstract: The Global Open Transient Telescope Array (GOTTA) project seeks to establish a coordinated network of more than a hundred 1-meter-class wide-field optical telescopes distributed worldwide. It will continuously monitor the entire night sky with a high cadence of less than one hour, searching for fast transients resulting from extreme astronomical explosions in the universe. The GOTTA Brain, an AI-based intelligent system, will manage the storage, computing and analysis of the vast datasets generated. GOTTA will advance scientific research by revealing the state of matter and the laws of physics under extreme conditions, shedding light on the structure and properties of spacetime in strong gravitational field, and providing insight into the history and expansion rate of our universe. GOTTA will welcome participants from all over the world and will make its data FAIRable to the public.

Items.Authors: Kensho Tanaka, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Kentaro Motohara, Shinobu Ozaki, Chihiro Tokoku, Kumiko Morihana, Yuki Moritani, Tomoya Yukino, Riku Sato, Michitoshi Yoshida
Items.Title: The optimization of NINJA infrared detector system
Items.Abstract: NINJA is an infrared spectrograph (0.8-2.5µm) for the Subaru Telescope optimized for Laser Tomography Adaptive Optics (LTAO) to achieve J_AB = 22 mag (S/N = 10, 2-hour exposure, R ~ 3000). The detector system of NINJA consists of a 2.5-µm cutoff HAWAII-2RG detector, a SIDECAR ASIC, and a MACIE interface board.   NINJA employs narrow slits (~0.35”) to exploit the sharp stellar images provided by LTAO. As a result, the contribution of readout noise becomes relatively large. Therefore, it is essential to optimize the detector system for realizing readout noise as low as 4 e⁻ rms. In this presentation, we describe how the reference voltages, bias voltages, gain settings and detector temperature affect the performance such as readout noise (CDS, Fowler sampling, and ramp-sampling), dynamic range, glow, and persistence. Through this optimization, we reach the readout noise of 4.0 e⁻ rms by 20 times Folwer sampling.

Items.Authors: Kuo-Chia (Alice) Liu, James Govern, Mark Melton, Lisa Bartusek, David Content, Michael Akkerman, Robert Campion, Carson McDonald
Items.Title: Integrated modeling for NASA's Roman Space Telescope: achieving unprecedented stability
Items.Abstract: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is the highest-priority large space mission identified by the 2020 New Worlds, New Horizon Decadal Survey in Astronomy and Astrophysics. To achieve its scientific objectives and technology demonstration goals, the observatory must meet unprecedented optical stability requirements. To this end, Roman built on the solid foundation established by the James Webb Space Telescope to successfully implement a system-level, cross-discipline analysis, or Integrated Modeling (IM), approach that marries system modeling and analysis with system engineering. Roman named IM a mission-enabling technology in recognition of its successful facilitation of error budget and requirement formulation, guidance for critical flight and test design decisions, and verification of key stability requirements through analysis. Future IM teams will need to continue to evolve as missions become increasingly complex, both technologically and in the scope of partner collaborations.

Items.Authors: Chad F. Bender, Roger Angel, Joel Berkson, Nina Brown, Erich Bugueno, Gilberto Chavez-Lopez, Sonja O. T. Choi, Megan Delamer, James Dibelka, Nick Didato, Trevor Dugan, Glen Douglass, Warren B. Foster, Kevin Gilliam, Peter Gray, Samuel Halverson, Yiyang Huang, Buell Jannuzi, Daewook Kim, Chris Kruep, Suvrath Mahadevan, Riley Mikkelsen, Andrew Monson, Chang Jin Oh, Fernando Parra, Jason Patrou, Milan Riha, Brian Scaramella, Christian Schwab, Melanie Sisco, William Thompson, Richard Wortley, Dennis Zaritsky, David Zeller
Items.Title: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope: status update of the prototype telescope
Items.Abstract: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope Project is designing and building a new optical telescope composed of an array of small “unit telescopes”, which can be replicated economically and at scale to produce an arbitrarily large incoherent aperture. Our first prototype telescope, the LFAST-20X, consists of twenty 0.76m, f/3.3 telescopes in a common frame, on a single altitude-azimuth mount, and has the equivalent collecting area of a traditional single aperture 3.5m telescope. In this talk, I will provide updates on the fabrication, assembly, and testing of the LFAST-20X, as well as describe our plans to operate this system as a working observatory after commissioning.

Items.Authors: Phillip M. Korngut
Items.Title: SPHEREx mission status after the first year of all-sky NIR spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: The SPHEREx space telescope is the newest NASA MIDEX mission, designed to study the Universe’s large-scale structure, probe the history of galaxy formation, and survey our Milky way for water and other biogenic ices. Full scale science operations began on May 1st, 2025 and two NIR spectroscopic surveys of the entire celestial sphere have been completed in the intervening year. In this update, we present the observatory’s operational status, instrumental performance and demonstrated sensitivity on-sky. The entirety of the spectral image data from these novel surveys will be made available to the community, with initial releases already available for public access.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Taralli, Martin De Wit, Roland Den Hartog, Davide Vaccaro, Pourya Khosropanah
Items.Title: Magnetic and mechanical stability of the Athena X-IFU focal plane assembly: results from the development model
Items.Abstract: We present magnetic-shielding and micro-vibration characterization of the X-IFU FPA Development Model for Athena space telescope. The FPA ensures a stable environment for the TES array at 50 mK using a multi-stage thermal suspension and a CMM–Nb shield. TESs act as sensitive magnetometers via their Fraunhofer-like response to perpendicular fields. Four Helmholtz coils installed inside the cryostat apply controlled AC/DC fields (<200 μT) without magnetizing the CMM. Preliminary results show a shielding factor ≥10⁵ at the detector plane, with the upgraded setup expected to increase this limit. Micro-vibrations in the 100–1000 Hz range are analyzed by correlating accelerometers on T2, thermometers across the FPA, and TES baseline variations. Resonant modes are identified, and their impact on thermal stability, dissipation, and detector noise is assessed to guide optimization of future FPA models.

Items.Authors: Taiki Bessho, Makoto Komaki, Yuji Ikeda, Masahito Uchiyama
Items.Title: Non-iterative random phase shifting interferometry via Fourier-domain reordering
Items.Abstract: Standard Temporal Phase-Shifting Interferometry (TPSI) is vulnerable to vibration, especially in large-scale metrology. We present a robust, non-iterative Random Phase Shift Interferometry (RPSI) technique utilizing Fourier-domain reordering. It reconstructs surfaces from random phase shifts without iteration. We demonstrate effectiveness by measuring an aspheric mirror of 1.3 m in diameter with an in-house interferometer and CGH. Where TPSI failed due to vibration ripples, our method achieved few-nanometer accuracy (PV). Unlike simultaneous phase-shifting with micro-polarizer arrays, our technique avoids array-induced systematic errors and polarization constraints. It eliminates the need for expensive piezoelectric actuators, enabling high-precision metrology even with semi-manual or wavelength shifting. We present the algorithm, validation on simulated and real data, and a dedicated Python-based module.

Items.Authors: Baolong Chen, Hong-fei Zhang, Xin Luo, Wei Liu, Zihao Xia, Qi Feng, Zhe Geng, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Development of a Software Framework for Automated Performance Test of Astronomical Cameras
Items.Abstract: Modern astronomical observation increasingly relies on large-format, high-sensitivity scientific-grade cameras, motivated by the testing demands of projects such as the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST) and Earth 2.0 (ET). Camera testing is an essential step in the design and manufacturing process of these scientific-grade cameras. However, existing testing processes often require users to manually set test conditions and analyze data, significantly reducing the efficiency of the manufacturing process. Therefore, we present PixelXVisionPlatform, an automated testing system that controls its components via a Software Development Kit (SDK). This system can autonomously acquire flat-field frames and dark frames while performing automated analysis of detector linearity, read noise, conversion gain, dark current, photo-response non-uniformity, and pixel defects. The results show that this approach significantly improves the testing efficiency of scientific-grade cameras.

Items.Authors: Szymon Gladysz, Andreas Zepp, Raphael Bellossi, Douglas McDonald, Marvin Schewe, Léonard Prengère, Joshua Morlot
Items.Title: Fast and scintillation-resistant wavefront sensing for laser applications
Items.Abstract: Propagating lasers through strong turbulence presents unique challenges that differ significantly from those of astronomical adaptive optics (AO). Therefore, unconventional approaches must be developed to meet these requirements. At Fraunhofer IOSB, several wavefront sensing concepts have either been invented or further developed for this purpose. Our work has focused on wavefront sensors (WFS) suitable for monochromatic light, i.e. lasers, and on achieving the highest possible bandwidth, as these sensors are primarily used for laser-based communications and energy delivery to and from fast-moving aircraft or satellites. This paper will focus on three such sensors: the holographic WFS, the heterodyne WFS and the angular transmission WFS.

Items.Authors: Howard Hui
Items.Title: SPHEREx survey progress and early observations
Items.Abstract: SPHEREx is the all sky near infrared survey launched on March 11 of 2025. We began full sky survey operations on May 1 of 2025 following two months of in orbit commissioning. The mission is designed to map the entire sky in 102 colors from 0.75 to 5 microns four times during the two year planned survey. In this talk I will describe the launch and in orbit commissioning activities. I will then provide an update on the performance of our calibrations and the current observation status. I will also show several examples of the science enabled by the early SPHEREx data release.

Items.Authors: Marcos Bavdaz, Sebastiaan Fransen, Ivo Ferreira, Pieter Smid, Marine Martin Lagarde, Habib Boualam, Alex McNamara, Frederic Safa, David Girou, Yvette Jenkins, Giuseppe Vacanti, Boris Landgraf, Maximilien J. Collon, Mark Olde Rieckerink, Jeroen Haneveld, Bart Schurink, Desiree Della Monica Ferreira, Sonny Massahi, Sara Svendsen, Diego Paredes Sanz, Michael Krumrey, Dieter Skroblin, Robert Fechner, Vadim Burwitz, Giovanni Pareschi, Bianca Salmaso, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Stefano Basso, Giuseppe Valsecchi, Dervis Vernani, George Floros, Mirko Riede, Tapio Korhonen, Mikko Pasanen, Alejandro Sanchez Grueso, Dominique Heinis, Joan Torras, Riccardo Bressan, Norman Niewrzella, Richard Willingale, Finn Christensen
Items.Title: Preparing the NewAthena X-ray optics implementation
Items.Abstract: The NewAthena (New Advanced Telescope for High ENergy Astrophysics) mission was endorsed by the ESA Science Program Committee in November 2023 and is currently being studied and technologically prepared for an adoption early 2027. It will be the next generation X-ray observatory, replacing the ageing Chandra and XMM Newton spacecraft, both in orbit since the previous century.    The challenge facing the NewAthena optics is the need to outperform any other existing X-ray optics technology by an order of magnitude, when combining high angular resolution and large effective area with a low mass.     The Silicon Pore Optics (SPO) delivers to this challenge and greatly benefits from technology spin-in from the semiconductor industry. The optics is highly modular and is robust by design, its production is largely automatised and therefore cost effective.    The paper will present the ongoing activities preparing the production of the NewAthena optics.

Items.Authors: Michele Cirasuolo, Suzanne Ramsay, Enrico Marchetti, Emanuela Ciattaglia, Diogo Rio Fernandes, Joel Vernet, Antoine Mérand, Celine Peroux, Andrea Capardi
Items.Title: The ESO Instrumentation Programme
Items.Abstract: The newly established ESO Instrumentation Programme brings together all instrumentation activities for the ELT, VLT, VLTI, and La Silla under a single coordinated framework. I will present the current status of the programme, highlighting major achievements including the delivery and commissioning of key VLT/VLTI instruments such as 4MOST, GRAVITY+, and MOONS, as well as an update on progress across the suite of ELT instruments. I will also outline the future roadmap of the programme and discuss the evolving landscape of current and next-generation ESO instrumentation, providing a vision for the scientific capabilities that will shape ESO’s future instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Daniel R. Harbeck, Kal Kadlec, Lisa Storrie-Lombardi, Nikolaus Volgenau, Norio Narita, Akihiko Fukui
Items.Title: An instrumentation update strategy for the Las Cumbres Observatory’s 1-meter telescope fleet
Items.Abstract: The Las Cumbres Observatory enables time domain astronomy with its fleet of 27 robotic 2-meter, 1-meter, and 0.35-meter telescopes. The telescopes are distributed at 7 sites to always access night skies. The use cases range from near earth objects, extrasolar planetary transits, Galactic stellar physics, active galactic nuclei, supernovae and multimessenger astrophysics.     The primary instruments on the fleet of 12 1-meter telescopes are legacy imagers based on Fairchild CCD486 detectors. Those cameras have reached the end of their useful life span, and in preparation for the Rubin Observatory LSST era we explored camera updates using commercial CMOS and CCD detectors, in single and dual channel designs. We review the instrument upgrade options we considered, and how they fit into science and operational requirements, as well into fiscal realities. We selected an upgrade to Princeton Instrument Sophia 4k deep depletion CCDs, and deployable dual chanel extension for two sites.

Items.Authors: Stefan J. Wijnholds
Items.Title: Computationally efficient, high-resolution, wide-FoV imaging with large-N-small-D arrays
Items.Abstract: At radio frequencies above ~1.5 GHz, arrays consisting of many small dishes (large-N-small-D) are a cost-effective way to create a large collecting area as illustrated by the DSA-2000. They also have the potential to combine the large Field-of-View (FoV) provided by the small dishes with a very high (~arcsecond) spatial resolution provided by the interferometric array as envisioned in the ARGOS project. Large-N-small-D interferometers can either be configured as a single array or as an array of subarrays. In this contribution, I assess the impact of this choice on the requirements (bandwidth and processing capacity) of the digital processing system needed to enable full-FoV, high-resolution imaging with the interferometer array. This shows that, for array of subarrays, the requirements on the digital processing system for imaging can be relaxed significantly by subarray beamforming.

Items.Authors: Esther Soria Hernandez, Manuel Collados, Angel Mato, Antonio Zamora, Ana María Marcos Martín, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Alvaro Perez Garcia
Items.Title: The polarimetric calibration and alignment assembly of the European Solar Telescope
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) is a next-generation 4.2 m solar facility designed to perform high-sensitivity spectropolarimetric observations of the solar atmosphere. To support the calibration, alignment, and verification activities required to achieve its scientific goals, the Polarimetric Calibration and Alignment (PCA) assembly has been developed around the Gregorian focal plane (F2). The PCA consists of four optomechanically independent levels distributed along the converging beam and integrates the Alignment Unit, the Polarimetric Calibration Unit, the ASM Figure Error Calibration Unit, the M7-DM Calibration Unit, and dedicated illumination sources. This contribution presents the preliminary design of the PCA and the optical and thermal analyses supporting its calibration performance and operational stability.

Items.Authors: Dervis Vernani, Giuseppe Valsecchi, Marcos Bavdaz, Ivo Ferreira, Pieter Smid, Habib Boualam, Alberto Moretti, Benjamin Kirm, Matej Papež, Janez Buh, Blaž Petkovšek
Items.Title: Assembly of mirror modules in the telescope structure of the NewAthena mission
Items.Abstract: Several hundred Silicon Pore Optics (SPO) Mirror Modules (MMs) shall be integrated and co-aligned onto the telescope structure of the NewAthena (New Advanced Telescope for High ENergy Astrophysics). Supported by ESA, Media Lario is designing and developing dedicated innovative facilities, capable of aligning, integrating and testing the NewATHENA mirror module assembly. The preparation of the NewAthena building at Media Lario premises is quite advanced. The building extends 6.5 m below ground and 17 m above ground. The building is dimensioned to accommodate, beside the UVOB facility, the vertical X-ray (VERT-X) test facility. The co-location of these two facilities is strategic for the NewATHENA, permitting regular X-ray measurements of the SPO MMs aligned and integrated with the UV light. The building is designed with a rail system connecting the two facilities, allowing the transfer of the telescope structure from the UVOB to VERT-X and vice versa.

Items.Authors: Elijah Anakalea-Buckley, Prakriti Gupta, David Hale, Michael Langmayr, COO Software Team
Items.Title: Modern Incident Management for Astronomical Observatories (Gecko)
Items.Abstract: Modern astronomical instruments rely on complex software and hardware, yet observers often lack time or tools to document system states during failures. Engineers must then reconstruct incomplete telemetry, logs, and UI states long after an event, slowing diagnosis and increasing downtime. We developed Gecko, a lightweight triage tool that captures a full snapshot of an instrument or telescope state with a single command. Gecko collects hardware and software logs, system metrics, active VNC interfaces, and provides a unified messaging interface for both CLI and GUI use. Current development includes a service-agnostic monitoring daemon for continuous health tracking with minimal overhead. Designed for generality and rapid deployment, Gecko introduces a modern, standardized approach to observatory debugging. Its goal is to work on any system while showing how intentional logging architecture makes triage and fault diagnosis straightforward, regardless of the tools used.

Items.Authors: Matthew R. Bolcar, John Hagopian, Alice Liu, Tyler Groff, Bente Eegholm, Alden Jurling, Matthew Bergkoetter, Joseph Howard, Guangjun Gao, Margaret Dominguez, Patricia Lyons, Cathy Marx, Scott Rohrbach, Olha Asmolova, Nicholas Bond, Nicholas Collins, John Crooke, Boris Glebov, Joseph Hayden, Samantha Herath, Mingjun Li, Timothy Reichard, Drew Siedel, Kaitlyn Summey, Greg Wenzel, Brian Kern, Mark Colavita, Gary Kuan
Items.Title: The Roman Space Telescope optical system: status, test, and verification - update
Items.Abstract: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (“Roman”) is NASA’s next flagship observatory. Launching in 2026, Roman will explore the nature of dark energy as well as expand the census of exoplanets in our galaxy via microlensing. Roman’s large field of view, agile survey capabilities, and excellent stability enable these scientific objectives, yet present unique challenges for the design, test, and verification of its optical system. Roman recently completed a comprehensive thermal vacuum test of the Spacecraft bus + Integrated Payload Assembly (SCIPA), followed by integrating the Outer Barrel Assembly (OBA), Solar Array Sunshield (SASS), and Deployable Aperture Cover (DAC) with SCIPA to complete the Observatory. This paper will present an overview of the thermal vacuum optical testing as well as a status of the optical system performance and verification.

Items.Authors: Paolo Chioetto, José Araiza-Durán, Umberto Barozzi, Lorenzo Barubiani, Andrea Bocchieri, Pasquale Bonfà, Daniele Brienza, Anna Brucalassi, Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Riccardo Claudi, Fabio D'Anca, Paul Eccleston, Alejandro Fernández-Soler, Debora Ferruzzi, Iacopo Ficai Veltroni, Manuele Gangi, Andrés García Pérez, Gabriele Grisoni, Elisa Guerriero, Riccardo Lilli, Lorenzo Maddii Fabiani, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Federico Miceli, Angelo Olivieri, Emanuele Pace, Enzo Pascale, Andrea Paternoster, Javier Pérez Álvarez, Paolo Picchi, Giampaolo Preti, Monica Rainer, Antonio Scippa, Giovanna Tinetti, Elisabetta Tommasi, Andrea Tozzi, Dervis Vernani, Paola Zuppella
Items.Title: Absolute reflectivity measurement for large telescope mirrors: setup and first insights
Items.Abstract: Accurate mirror reflectivity is crucial for predicting telescope performance. For Ariel’s primary mirror (M1) Engineering Model, an absolute reflectivity measurement setup was developed to obtain values directly from the coated surface and validate sample-based results. The system uses a broadband light source, integrating sphere with spectrometer, and a custom configuration to compare incident and reflected intensities. Mounted on a dedicated structure, it ensures safe handling of large mirrors in various orientations. Verified with reference mirrors, the setup showed good repeatability. Measurements on multiple M1 positions provide an independent benchmark for optical models and confirm feasibility of in-situ characterization.
